segments.html: Python selects a random number between 1 and 5. We have to run the program multiple times until we guess it.
segments.text: Python selects a random number between 1 and 5. We have to run the program multiple times until we guess it.

segments.html: What if we want to allow them to continue to guess, within a single run of the program? We use a while loop, which allows us to repeat some code as long as a particular condition remains true.
segments.text: What if we want to allow them to continue to guess, within a single run of the program? We use a while loop, which allows us to repeat some code as long as a particular condition remains true.

import random
secret=random.randint(1,5)

print("I've picked a secret number between 1 and 5.")
guess=0 # set it to zero so the following line will be true the first time

# this code repeats until the condition is false
# that is,
while (secret!=guess):
  # beginning of indented block of statements associated with the "while"
  guess=int(input("What is your guess?"))
  if (guess>5) or (guess<1):
    print("Your guess wasn't between 1 and 5.")
    print("Try again.")
  elif secret!=guess:
    print("Sorry, you guessed wrong. Try again.")
  # end of statements associated with the while

print("You got it!")

items: They start by evaluating the boolean expression that follows the word "while"
If the expression is false, the block of statements associated with the while loop is not executed, and the program continues below them.
If the expression is true, the block of statements associated with the while loop is executed, and then step (1) above is repeated.

segments.html: The two types of loops in Python are while loops and for loops. In both types of loops, one pass through the block of statements indented under the loop is called an iteration. For instance, if the block is executed five times, the loop is said to have executed five iterations.

segments.html: In the following example, of an effectively infinite loop, we use an accumulator variable. An accumulator variable i is a variable that is increased inside the loop.
segments.text: In the following example, of an effectively infinite loop, we use an accumulator variable. An accumulator variable i is a variable that is increased inside the loop.

# not an infinite loop, but effectively one.
# initialize i to zero
i=0
# set upper limit to one trillion (10 to the 12th power)
limit=1000000000000
# print it using an f string with comma separators
print(f"{limit:,d}")
while(i<limit):
  # increment i by one
  i+=1
  # print every ten million
  if (i%10000000)==0: print(f"{i:,d}")

segments.html: Here's a program that adds up numbers in succession and then stops when the sum is greater than or equal to 1000.

  # not an infinite loop because this gets us out
  if total>1000: break

segments.html: The continue statement allows you to go to the next iteration of the loop in the middle of the block of statements in the loop.
segments.text: The continue statement allows you to go to the next iteration of the loop in the middle of the block of statements in the loop.

segments.html: For instance, suppose we want to print all of the numbers from 1 to 5, but we want to skip 3. Here's how we can use continue to do that:
segments.text: For instance, suppose we want to print all of the numbers from 1 to 5, but we want to skip 3. Here's how we can use continue to do that:

i=0
# note the last iteration is when i is initially 4,
# since it then adds one to i to make it 5
# and then
while (i<=4):
  i+=1
  # if i is 3, go back to the top of the loop
  if i==3: continue
  print(i)

segments.html: The following simulates a rock/paper/scissors tournament between you and the computer. The game ends when either side gets three wins.
segments.text: The following simulates a rock/paper/scissors tournament between you and the computer. The game ends when either side gets three wins.

import random
computerWins=0
userWins=0
while (computerWins<3) and (userWins<3):
  computerChoice=random.randint(1,3)
  userChoice=int(input("Enter your choice: rock (1), paper (2), or scissors (3)"))
  print("Computer chose ",end='')
  if computerChoice==1:
    print("rock.")
  elif computerChoice==2:
    print("paper.")
  else:
    print("scissors.")
  difference=computerChoice-userChoice
  if difference==0:
    print("It's a tie.")
  # computer win scenarios
  # either choice is one greater than user choice
  # scissors cuts paper, paper wraps rock
  # or computer chose rock, user scissors
  # which means the difference is -2
  elif (difference==1) or (difference==-2):
    print("The computer won.")
    computerWins+=1
  # otherwise user won
  else:
    print("You won.")
    userWins+=1
print("\nTournament Results:")
print(f"You won {userWins} times.")
print(f"The computer won {computerWins} times.")

slides.title: Flipping a Coin Until You Get Five Heads in a Row

segments.html: How many coin flips does it take until you get five heads in a row? Well, it varies!
segments.text: How many coin flips does it take until you get five heads in a row? Well, it varies!

import random
headsInARow=0
nFlips=0
headsRequired=5
while headsInARow<headsRequired:
  nFlips+=1
  if random.randint(1,2)==1: # consider a one a head
    headsInARow+=1
    print("H",end="")
  else:
    print("T",end="")
    headsInARow=0
  if (nFlips%30==0): print()
print(f"\nIt took {nFlips} flips to get {headsRequired} heads in a row.")

segments.html: In the game of Nim, there are two players and initially seven sticks. On each player's turn, they may pick up up to three sticks. The player who picks up the final stick loses.
segments.text: In the game of Nim, there are two players and initially seven sticks. On each player's turn, they may pick up up to three sticks. The player who picks up the final stick loses.

segments.html: This can be implemented by a nested while loop as follows.
segments.text: This can be implemented by a nested while loop as follows.

# initially there are seven sticks
sticksLeft=7
while (sticksLeft>0):
  # start with player 1
  player=1
  while True: # outer infinite while loop that we will break out of
    # print out the number of sticks left
    print(f"There are {sticksLeft} sticks left.")
    # inner while loop- one player's turn
    while True: # inner infinite while loop that we will break out of
      sticksTaken=int(input(f"Player {player}, how many sticks do you want to pick up?"))
      # if they selected a valid number of sticks, 1-3 and no more than the number left
      if (sticksTaken<=sticksLeft) and (sticksTaken>=1) and (sticksTaken<=3):
        # take away the sticks they selected
        sticksLeft-=sticksTaken
        # check if the game is over: if so, set a flag that it is.
        gameOver=(sticksLeft==0)
        # if the game is over print out who lost by taking the last stick
        if gameOver:
          print(f"No sticks left. Player {player} lost.")
        # end the turn of this player by breaking out of the inner while loop
        break
      # otherwise get them to enter their choice again
      else:
       print("Invalid entry. Try again.")
    #change player
    if player==1:
      player=2
    else:
      player=1
    #  if the game is over break out of the outer while loop as well
    if gameOver: break

slides.title: Another way to look at 𝑒

segments.html: Another way to look at 𝑒 is as the result of compounding interest. If you have one dollar invested at 100% interest for a year, then after a year you have two dollars. However, if this is compounded twice (50% after six months and another 50% after a year), you get 1.5 squared or $2.25. If it is compounded four times, you get 1.25 to the fourth power, or about $2.44. In the limit, when it is compounded continously (an infinite number of times) you get 𝑒 dollars; 𝑒 is about 2.718 (but is an irrational number with an infinite number of non-repeating digits after the decimal point.)

i=0
# initially we have one (dollar)
initialAmount=1
resultingAmount=initialAmount
# compound numberCompounds times
while (i<numberCompounds):
  resultingAmount*=compoundingRate
  i+=1
print(resultingAmount)
print(math.e)
